properties.scope: item, event, interest, person, group, place, reference
properties.trigger: user mentions vinyl records, LPs, or singles, their record collection or wantlist, buying, pre-ordering, selling, trading, or lending records, record stores, crate digging, or Record Store Day, pressings, record condition and grading, or cleaning records, or spinning or listening to a record

data.short_description: Vinyl Tracker mini-app — a record collector's log. Tracks each physical copy as an item with optional collector-grade format, pressing, Goldmine condition, package completeness, and cleaning details; a wantlist with grails, grade floors, and price limits; pre-orders; Record Store Day prep; duplicates, trade bait, and upgrades; what was paid and where; spins as events with ratings; loans, sales, trades, and gifts as handoff events; provenance; and first-class artist entities (CREATED_BY). Full operating rules are in this entity's lore chunks: Data Model: Records, Data Model: Artists/Shops/Events, Collection & Wantlist, Spins/Condition/Care, Loans/Sales/Trades, Queries & Stats. Read all lore before acting on record-related requests.

lore.title: Data Model: Records
lore.content:
RECORD = item entity (item_type: "vinyl_record", tag "vinyl-tracker"), one per physical copy the user owns, wants, or has pre-ordered — not one per album. Other apps' items share the namespace, so check item_type on any name hit.

NAMING. Slugs derive from names: never rename an existing record; only the new arrival gets a suffix.
- Default: the album title ("Rumours"). A wanted or pre-ordered record for a specific pressing carries it from the start ("Rumours (1977 UK Original)").
- Name taken by an item that isn't a copy of this album (a movie, a book, another album): add the artist, then the year if still taken ("Purple Rain (Prince)", "Weezer (Weezer, 1994)").
- Another copy of the same album (owned, wanted, or pre-ordered): add its pressing ("Rumours (2011 Reissue)"), or "Copy 2", "Copy 3" when unknown or identical.

FIELDS. Album fields come from general knowledge. Every other field comes only from the user or a page they share, never a guess, because copies of one album differ; leave unknowns unset. To clear a field, set it to null. Array edits replace the whole array, so read it first. Keep status out of the description; it lives in properties.
- Album: album (canonical title, never suffixed, shared by every copy), artist (as billed), original_year, genres (array), release_type ("album" | "ep" | "single" | "compilation" | "live" | "soundtrack").
- Format: size ("12in" | "10in" | "7in"), discs, rpm (33 | 45 | 78), box_set.
- Pressing: label, catalog_number, pressing_year (a number; leave unset if only the decade is known), country (common short name: "UK", "US", "Japan"), edition ("original" | "reissue" | "repress" | "remaster" | "limited" | "promo" | "test_pressing"), variant (free text: "180g black"), matrix (runout etchings, verbatim), numbered ("0412/1000"), signed, pressing_notes (free text for what the fields can't hold: "1980s Columbia repress", "Tone Poet series"), exclusive_to ("RSD <YYYY>" | "RSD Black Friday <YYYY>" | "tour" | "webstore" | "club" | "shop_exclusive"; describes the release, not where this copy was bought).
- Condition: media_grade and sleeve_grade (Goldmine: "M" | "NM" | "VG+" | "VG" | "G+" | "G" | "F" | "P"), sealed, condition_notes (an array of "YYYY-MM-DD: note" strings, appended, never overwritten).
- Package: includes and missing, arrays from "inner_sleeve" | "insert" | "lyric_sheet" | "booklet" | "poster" | "print" | "obi" | "hype_sticker" | "download_code" (missing unset = unknown; [] = complete, set only when the user confirms); download_code_status ("unused" | "redeemed" | "expired").
- Care: last_cleaned (ISO date), cleaning_method, needs_cleaning.
- Listening: favorite_tracks (array).
- State: status ("wanted" | "preordered" | "owned" | "sold" | "traded" | "given_away" | "lost"), favorite, on_loan, for_trade, upgrade_wanted with upgrade_notes, storage_location.
- Acquisition: purchase_date (the item's built-in field: the day the user got this copy, however they got it; default today), acquired_how ("bought" | "gift" | "trade" | "inherited" | "found"), price_paid with currency (ISO code, the user's usual one), bought_new, purchased_from (seller name; for a tracked shop, its exact entity name). An in-stock mail order is owned from the day it's bought.
- Pre-order (status "preordered": paid for before release or stock): ordered_date, expected_ship_date (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM), price_paid, currency, purchased_from, acquired_how "bought", bought_new: true. purchase_date is set on arrival.
- Wantlist (status "wanted"): the copy fields describe the copy sought; min_grade (a Goldmine grade), must_include (package vocabulary), max_price (in currency), want_priority ("grail" | "high" | "normal"), want_notes (anything else).
- Departure: gone_date, sale_price with sale_currency, sale_channel. Never delete a record that has left; its history stays.

NO MARKET VALUE: never set the built-in value property or estimate a record's worth. Records never store a rating; ratings live on spins.

LINKS: every record RELATED_TO interest/record_collecting and CREATED_BY its artists; REFERENCES a reference entity for a release page the user shares (never invent URLs).

FINDING. Records are items tagged "vinyl-tracker"; spins and handoffs are events with that tag (event_type "vinyl_spin" | "vinyl_handoff"). Search results lack properties: call get_entities before filtering or summing. Gather an album's copies by filtering properties.album and checking artist. Before naming a new record, also search all items by name without the tag filter.

lore.title: Data Model: Artists, Shops & Events
lore.content:
ARTIST: a solo artist is a person (person_type "human", occupation "musician"); a band is a group (group_type "band"). Search first and create once. Tag only artists this app creates, ["artist", "vinyl-tracker"]; reuse an artist another app created as is, without changing its tags or occupation. The artist tag keeps public figures apart from contacts: never link an artist socially to the owner unless the user knows them. Each record links CREATED_BY every credited artist; a joint billing ("Prince and the Revolution") links both the lead artist (person) and the band (group); "Various Artists" compilations get no edge.

SHOP: a place (place_type "shop") for a named store or fair the user buys from in person. Search first and create once, naming a chain's branch as the user does ("Rough Trade East"); tag "vinyl-tracker" only if this app creates it. If the owner has no VISITED or FREQUENTS edge to it, create owner VISITED shop with the edge's started set to the date, and never touch those edges again. Online sellers are not places: purchased_from only. There is no record-to-shop edge.

SPIN: an event, created only when the user mentions one. Name "Spun <record name> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)"; if taken, append the time when known, otherwise " #2", " #3". Properties: event_type "vinyl_spin", date plus date_year/date_month/date_day, rating (1-10, optional), impression, first_spin, sides. Tag "vinyl-tracker". Links: RELATED_TO the record; each listener ATTENDED (always the owner); OCCURRED_AT a place only when away from home.

HANDOFF: an event for a record changing hands with someone the user knows. Always for a loan; for a gift, a purchase from a person, a sale, a trade, or a give-away only when the other party is known (anonymous buyers and sellers stay in purchased_from or sale_channel). Name "<Lent | Received | Bought | Sold | Traded | Gave Away> <record name> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)", deduped like spins; a trade is named for the outgoing record. Properties: event_type "vinyl_handoff", handoff ("loan" | "gift_in" | "bought_from" | "sale" | "trade" | "gift_out"), date plus date_year/date_month/date_day, returned (loans only; unset while out), note. Tag "vinyl-tracker". Links: RELATED_TO each record that moved; the other person and the owner ATTENDED.

TRADES: the incoming record RELATED_TO the outgoing one { role: "traded_for", date }, whether or not the partner is known.

PEOPLE THE USER KNOWS (listeners, borrowers, givers, buyers, partners): create one only after confirming who they are, and don't tag them: they are the user's contacts, not app data. When the user says how they know them, link owner FRIENDS_WITH (a friend) or KNOWS (anyone else), once.

PROVENANCE: a record with a story (inherited, signed, bought from its original owner) gets a lore chunk titled exactly "Provenance", one line per handoff, newest last. Read it before adding a line; lore updates replace the whole chunk.

lore.title: Workflow: Collection & Wantlist
lore.content:
ADD A RECORD ("picked up X at Y for $25").
1. Search for the artist and the album's copies. Work through these in order: a preordered copy → ask whether this is it (yes: Arrival, done; no: go on); a wanted copy → Found It; an owned copy → ask whether this is another pressing or an identical duplicate.
2. Create the record, status "owned", with what the user gave (purchase_date defaults to today). Bought in person with no shop named: ask once which; if they'd rather not say, leave purchased_from empty.
3. Link per Links; create or reuse the shop; create a handoff (gift_in or bought_from) when a known person gave or sold it.
4. Offer once, in one line: new or used (if unsaid), format, pressing, grades, package, or a release page, and for a used copy whether it needs cleaning. Take what's given; album and artist alone is enough.
5. Confirm in one line: title, artist, pressing if known, price, where.

BULK ADD (a list, a photo of spines). Search first. Create artists and records (album fields only) with create_entities, up to 100 per call, skip_existing on; then edges with create_relationships, skip_duplicates on, only for entities actually created or confirmed — a skipped name may belong to another app. Report what was added, skipped, and ambiguous (self-titled albums, unclear artists).

WANTLIST ("hunting for X"). Search first. A better copy of a record they own is upgrade_wanted on that copy, not a wanted record; a wanted record is for an album they don't own or a specific other pressing. Never track one hunt both ways. Create it with the Wantlist fields: "VG+ or better" → min_grade, "must have the OBI" → must_include, "original 1977 UK" → edition, pressing_year, country; priority defaults to "normal". To list: wanted records, grails first.

FOUND IT. Convert the wanted record in place: status "owned", acquisition fields as in Add, the sought copy fields replaced with this copy's (clear any it lacks), wantlist fields cleared. If the copy falls short (copy fields differ from those sought, grade under min_grade, a must_include item missing), ask whether the hunt continues; if it does, the find is a new owned record and the wanted one stays; if not, convert in place. If they own other copies, clear their upgrade_wanted and ask what happens to them (Upgrade).

PRE-ORDER. Search first as in Add. Create it per the Pre-order fields plus any announced copy fields (variant, numbered, exclusive_to); shop as in Add. A wanted copy of the same album: if the pre-order is what was sought, convert that record in place to the pre-order (as in Found It, but status "preordered"); if it falls short, ask whether the hunt continues — yes: the pre-order is a new record and the wanted one stays; no: convert in place.

ARRIVAL ("my X pre-order came"). If several match, ask which. Set status "owned" and purchase_date (default today), clear expected_ship_date, then make the Add step 4 offer.

CANCELLED PRE-ORDER. Ask whether they still want it. Yes: status "wanted" with want_priority "normal" (currency kept); clear ordered_date, expected_ship_date, price_paid, purchased_from, acquired_how, and bought_new. No: delete it after they confirm (it never entered the collection).

RELEASE PAGE (a Discogs or similar link). Read it and propose the copy fields it shows, package contents included; if it lists several matrices, ask which is on their copy. Write only what they confirm, never overwrite their earlier answers without asking, and link REFERENCES a reference entity for the URL (search first).

RECORD STORE DAY PREP (the RSD list, pasted or linked). Ask which releases they want and add each via Wantlist, with exclusive_to "RSD <YYYY>" (or "RSD Black Friday <YYYY>") and priority defaulting to "high".

AT THE SHOP ("what should I look for?"). List RSD wants on the day, then grail and high-priority wants with min_grade, must_include, max_price, and want_notes, then upgrade_wanted copies with upgrade_notes; mention how many are for_trade if the shop takes trade-ins. Asked about a specific record, first say whether they own a copy, with its pressing and grade.

EDITS. "One of my favorites" → favorite: true; "I'd trade X" → for_trade: true; "I want a better copy of X" → upgrade_wanted with upgrade_notes. Corrections update the record's properties.

lore.title: Workflow: Spins, Condition & Care
lore.content:
LOG A SPIN ("spinning X with Sam").
1. Find the copy: one owned copy → use it; several → ask once; only a pre-order → it arrived, run Arrival first; owned but untracked → offer Add a Record; not their copy (a friend's, a stream) → no spin, and if they loved it, offer the wantlist.
2. Create the spin; first_spin: true when the record has none earlier.
3. On a first spin, ask for a 1-10 rating and a one-line impression if not given; on later spins, record a rating only when offered. Remarks about condition ("the crackle") → offer a dated condition note.
4. Link per the Data Model, creating people per People the User Knows. Confirm in one line.

CONDITION ("side B skips"). Append a dated note to condition_notes. Change a grade only when the user gives one.

CLEANING ("cleaned the Blue Note stack"). Set last_cleaned (default today), cleaning_method if given, and needs_cleaning: false. For a named group, list the records you take it to mean and confirm first. "X needs cleaning" → needs_cleaning: true.

FAVORITE TRACKS. Add to favorite_tracks (read it first). Defects on a track go in condition_notes.

RE-RATE ("actually Rumours is a 10"). Update the album's most recent rated spin, on any copy unless they say which; if no spin is rated, the most recent spin. With no spins, ask whether to log one for when they last listened; never invent one.

"WHAT DID I THINK OF X?" The album's most recent rated spin, plus how many times it has been spun.

lore.title: Workflow: Loans, Sales, Trades
lore.content:
LEND ("Sam borrowed X"). Status stays "owned"; set on_loan: true and create a loan handoff.

RETURN. Set on_loan: false and returned on the open loan handoff (handoff "loan", RELATED_TO this record, no returned date). Keep the event as history.

WHO HAS MY RECORDS? Open loan handoffs: the borrower (the attendee who isn't the owner), the record, and how long it has been out. Say plainly when a loan is over three months old, without nagging.

SELL ("sold X on Discogs for $40"). Status "sold", gone_date, sale_price, sale_currency, sale_channel. A sale handoff when the buyer is someone the user knows.

TRADE ("traded my X for Sam's Y"). Outgoing record: status "traded", gone_date. Incoming record: via Add a Record with acquired_how "trade" and no price. Link the traded_for edge, plus one trade handoff on both records when the partner is known.

GIVE AWAY, LOSE, OR BREAK. Status "given_away" (a gift_out handoff when the recipient is known) or "lost" (broken too; add a dated note on how), with gone_date.

UPGRADE ("replaced my beat-up copy"). The new copy is a new owned record, named per Naming. Clear upgrade_wanted and upgrade_notes on the old copy and ask its fate: Sell, Give Away, Lost, or keep both.

PROVENANCE. When a record arrives or leaves with a story, add a line per the Data Model.

lore.title: Workflow: Queries & Stats
lore.content:
"The collection" means status "owned" (on loan included); wanted, pre-ordered, and departed records are left out of it but stay searchable. Find records per Finding. Never add different currencies together: report each separately. Count empty fields as "unknown". Answer conversationally; use a table only for 4+ records.

- "Do I have X?" → every copy of the album, with status, pressing, grade, completeness, and storage_location; say plainly if it has left ("you sold it in March 2025").
- "What do I have by <artist>?" → query_relationships (neighbors) on the artist → CREATED_BY records. Never string-match the artist property.
- Counts and breakdowns (genre, decade from original_year, release_type, size, label, edition) → owned records, grouped.
- "What did I spend this year?" → price_paid where acquired_how is "bought", dated by ordered_date for pre-orders (arrived or not) and purchase_date otherwise, records since sold included; name any outstanding pre-orders in the total. Sales are a separate figure (net only if asked).
- "What has my collection cost?" → price_paid over owned records. Asked what it's worth: give the cost and say market value isn't tracked.
- "Where do I buy most?" → bought records grouped by purchased_from, with count and spend.
- Most-played / highest-rated → spins counted per record / spins sorted by rating.
- "What should I spin?" → three different albums (one copy each) from owned records not on loan or needing cleaning. Favor never or long-unspun ones, weighted toward artists and genres of spins rated 8 or higher, with a favorite mixed in; say why each fits, naming a favorite track if recorded. If fewer than three qualify, say so.
- "Wantlist under $30?" → max_price at or under it in the same currency, or none set; show min_grade and must_include.
- "Outstanding pre-orders?" → status "preordered", with seller and expected_ship_date; flag any overdue.
- Cleaning → needs_cleaning: true; "never cleaned" → no last_cleaned.
- "Duplicates" / "more than one copy" → owned copies grouped by album and artist, 2+, with pressing, grade, for_trade, and which are identical (matching pressing fields).
- Trade bait → for_trade. Upgrades → upgrade_wanted with upgrade_notes. Incomplete → non-empty missing. Unused codes → download_code_status "unused".
- "What did Sam give me?" / "What have I traded with Sam?" → their ATTENDED edges to vinyl_handoff events, by handoff, then RELATED_TO the records.
- Insurance inventory → every owned record: artist, title, label, catalog_number, country, pressing_year, matrix, grades, price_paid with currency, purchase_date, purchased_from, storage_location. A table, or CSV if asked, with the cost total per currency, and one line saying these are purchase costs, not replacement values.
- Year in review → acquisitions by purchase_date year (count, top shop, first and last) with spend dated as above, spins by date_year (count, most-spun record, top artist, best first spin), departures by gone_date year.

data.short_description: Collection anchor for the Vinyl Tracker app. All record items link here via RELATED_TO so the full collection can be queried from one hub.
